Exercise: Floor Glute-Ham Raise

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
intermediate

Movement Patterns:

- eccentric_concentric

Primary Muscles:

- hamstrings

Secondary Muscles:

- calves
- glutes

Equipment:
None

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
ATP-PC and glycolytic

Recovery Time:
48 hours

Goals:

- hypertrophy_of_the_hamstrings_and_glutes
- strengthening_of_the_core_and_stabilizing_muscles

Contraindications:

- Recent hamstring injury or surgery
- Severe lower back pain

Exercise Variations:

- name: Partner Assisted, instructions: Use a partner to hold your feet during the movement.
- name: Knee Flexion Variation, instructions: Keep knees slightly bent throughout the exercise to reduce strain on the hamstrings.

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Romanian Deadlift, equipment: barbell
- exercise_name: Single-Leg Glute-Ham Raise, equipment: None

Instructions:

- You can use a partner for this exercise or brace your feet under something stable.
- Begin on your knees with your upper legs and torso upright. If using a partner, they will firmly hold your feet to keep you in position. This will be your starting position.
- Lower yourself by extending at the knee, taking care to NOT flex the hips as you go forward.
- Place your hands in front of you as you reach the floor. This movement is very difficult and you may be unable to do it unaided. Use your arms to lightly push off the floor to aid your return to the starting position.
